items.note: K1/K1.a state the lemma (y_S <- y_S + x_S for arbitrary scratch, three stages give (X_a,Y_a) -> (-Y_a,X_a), scratch restored) and K1.a.1-K1.b follow the proof at 741-765 exactly (net change (JV+RG)x, coefficients |S cap T| mod 2 and (|S cap T|-1)/2, stage sequence). The sizes h=100, N, m and the wire counts W_b, W_c (767-783) are never given, but the lemma's proof is complete.

K2 states D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1} with frames on every incidence, and K2.a-K2.c reproduce the invariant argument of 804-825 (stored = D_v applied to logical, common frame commutes with pointwise gate, route operator eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1} on auxiliary roles too). KS.frame applies it with address shears as at 1514-1518.

The lemma's conclusions are stated correctly (comparable labels, only central 3->4 edges decrease by h, L=Ich, sum of |Delta dim| = Wm-2N+2L, L_b/N=100/539, L_c/N=101/539), but the labels themselves (subspaces of F^{tensor 3} built from triple indicators, orthogonal for neighbours, the gate-label table 975-988) and the orthonormal-basis clause are missing. Only the telescoping half of the proof (1066-1071) is shown; the residual table (1012-1064) that establishes nestedness and the single decreasing edge is not.

The rank sum s_b = W_b m - N + 2L_b < W_b m is derived faithfully (rank of P_V-P_U equals the dimension change; the N source edges 2P_{U_a} of rank one; deficit N-2L_b), and KS.frame states the endpoint identity with frames Phi_M giving H <- H+D. The verification of the endpoint identity (P_{U_a^perp} + P_{U_a} = I_m, zero source and identity sink elsewhere, 1169-1171) is missing.

The plan states the per-edge product of one kernel aI+bX_v per orthonormal residual vector, the s_c child count and C^{tensor e} on every role after corrections, but never defines the phase frames C_U = H^{tensor m} diag(i^{wt(P_U x)}) H^{tensor m} and never gives s_c = W_c m - 2N + 2L_c < W_c m. The one-line method does not follow the proof (weight additivity mod 4, odd weights, Z corrections on the 27 support coordinates).

L/N<1/2 giving s_b<W_b m (K3.A.3, K3.B.4) and the exponent argument (deficit > 20*2^{-50}, log m<20, m^{1-2^{-50}} > m(1-20*2^{-50}) > m(1-eta)) follow 1105-1110 and 1331-1344. The explicit deficits eta_b, eta_c are not given, and the complex case s_c<W_c m (deficit 2N-2L_c) is not stated separately, only used implicitly through sigma in S3.3.e.

S2.1 states the elementary stream operations correctly. S2.2 drops the hypothesis that the offset be preparable in b^{O(1)} time from the claim itself (it is only in the quote) and attributes the two-piece split-and-merge to unit multiplication as well, which the paper does with c pieces (592-608). No sub-steps derive either lemma.

K4 states A=E_1 Pi E_2 correctly and K5.a-K5.c follow the shear proof exactly (triangular changes by controlled shifts, E_2 and E_1^{-1}, the three-update interchange, exactly a interchanges). The elimination proof of the factorization (1375-1392) is not given, and the choice of the fixed odd prime q avoiding the table's denominators (1413-1423) is absent.

Every stage of the paper's proof is present: k=0 base, cyclic row split into W streams of volume V/W, shear frames with the endpoint condition, the three-update interchange, s recursive calls, F_k <= (s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) with its two-case geometric sum, the depth-first parking schedule and descriptor bound. The row-field divisibility hypothesis is supplied in S2.3 rather than in KS itself.

S2.3-S2.6 follow 1649-1734: rho=O(log e) high digits as the row field, padding to a multiple of W^k, base-m pieces with power-width calls, the geometric sum O(V e^tau), and padding binary ranges to [q^e]. The field-joining moves are condensed and the unequal-width remark (1740-1762) is omitted, neither essential to the lemma.

The identities, the per-edge kernel product, the inverse child (C^{-1})^{tensor f} = (-i)^f Z C Z, the s_c children on f=e/m axes and H_0^{tensor D} = b^D S_D C^{tensor D} S_D are all there. The central device, conjugation by the binary change of basis P_M that moves the residual directions to coordinate slots (1848-1865), and the slot/column layout with row additions from Gaussian elimination (1867-1901) are only alluded to as 'binary changes of basis'.

Follows the proof step by step: the eight conditional +-1 updates and their net map, whole-chunk cyclic shifts with target-independent offsets, the guard-based bad set with delta_bad = min{1, 80(f-1)2^{-K}}, T_0 S_0^{-1} permuting B, sort-based repair and the final two-bit XOR, giving O(V(L^tau+1)) in the family.

Node overhead O(V((eK)^tau+1)), rows from the first q_0 chunks with padding to W^{k_0}, F(e) <= (s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1) with F(e)=O(e) at leaves, internal sum O(e^lambda), leaf bound O(e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}) and the base-m pieces giving O(d^{lambda'}) all match 2286-2445.

States Q_p(Hz) in O(V d^{lambda'}) with error < sqrt2 2^{-p} and one truncation, and derives the guard width through A(e) <= sA(e/m)+E, A(e) <= 8B^2 d^{nu+1}, the depth-to-grid induction and Delta = ceil(C_0 d^{C_1}) = o(p), plus the row-sum-one disk argument, as in 2479-2586 and 2741-2757.

Character cancellation by the index shift, decimation in frequency with bit-reversed storage B_t and the reversed procedure giving F_t^+ B_t^{-1}, the grouped round with J_E, and the layout L (prefix slots, at most Dq-1 width-K exchanges), cost O(Tp[dK+pK^{tau-1}+l d^{lambda'}]), error < sqrt2 l 2^{-p} and exact operators L B F^- and F^+ B^{-1} L^{-1} all match the paper.

Evaluation at B_0=2^{4p}, the separation |h_j| <= r2^{2p} < B_0/2, centered extraction with carry in {0,1}, the numerator streams ac-be and ae+bc reduced mod y^r+1 and the shift by p+l bits follow 3233-3365.

Two forward transforms kept in LB order, pointwise products, the opposite procedure and the exact scale by M; the normalization identity, P(LBu,LBv) = LB P(u,v) and the 3delta+eta error bound reproduce 3414-3473.

The derivation follows the paper (Gaussian identity and Neumann inverse of N, A=S' and B_0=D'J'C, normalizations 2^{-2alpha^2}, tensoring with gamma=2d alpha^2, per-line costs, O(d^2) chunk-swap axis moves). The permutations P_s, P_t are never defined, and the approximation guarantees (error < p^2 per line, dp^2 tensorwise) and the hypotheses gcd(s,t)=1, theta>p/alpha^4 appear only scattered (S6.1.f).

Both identities and their proofs (coefficient comparison, R F^+ R = F^+ via h=ck for a unit, the convolution rule giving (u*v)/S^2) match 3938-3983. The chirp a_j = exp(-pi i sum s_i j_i^2/t_i) is never defined, so the first identity is stated with an unspecified kernel.

Fixed exponents, b, p=6b, d, K, T, the size consequences, the prime-interval count with eta=1/(4d), T/2<S<T by Bernoulli, alpha^4 theta_i > 3db >= p, and no wraparound with c_j < 2^{3b} all match. The n^{o(1)} prime search is not mentioned.
Algebra map, order-S argument, triangular coordinates b_i = a_i + mu_i sum_{j<i} a_j P_j mod s_i, update order i=d..1 and the O(Tp d^2(1+l^tau)) cost reproduce 4204-4292.

The exact isomorphism and wrap check are derived as at 4303-4347. The computed procedure (f' = Q_p(theta^+ f), h' via the ring convolution, untwist, 4374-4392) that the pack's derivation range covers is not described; only its error total appears in S6.6.b.

Source transform A, computed chirp, B_0, scale 2^gamma with exact counterpart R F_s and the conjugated opposite procedure; the six steps including the two S scalings and rounding match 4454-4544. The digit scaling 2^{-b-2} is implicit only through 2^{2b+4}.
E_ring < 5TL, the twisted convolution < 6TL, chirp < 8TL, E_s = 9*2^gamma TL, E_w < 28*2^gamma T^2 L, final error < 448b 2^{-3b/4} < 1/2, rounding and carry recurrence all match the paper.

Reproduces the table's seven normalized costs and powers, the margins with min g_2 = 2^{-181} = 2 kappa, the row justifications, the o(Tp) setup and the final O(n (log n)^{1-kappa}) with the schoolbook cutoff.
S0 lists n-log-n-conjecture among its prerequisites but no step says why the bound refutes an eventual c_A n lg n lower bound (liminf T_A(n)/(n lg n) = 0).

errors.says: Adding an offset from earlier controls to a later field mod q^b, or multiplying it by a fixed unit, costs O(V) by splitting each fibre into two pieces and merging them in the opposite order.
errors.paper: The O(V) bound for the offset update holds only if the offset can be prepared in b^{O(1)} time; the two-piece split and merge is the offset update, while multiplication by a unit c uses c increasing pieces and negation a stack reversal.

errors.says: Each packed line is a single whole-chunk cyclic shift, a bijection costing O(V) after one chunk swap by controlled shifts.
errors.paper: Each rotation first moves its target chunk to the rightmost position by a chunk swap costing O(V L^tau) (Lemma chunk-swap), then performs the O(V) controlled shift, then undoes the swap; the swap is not done by controlled shifts.

chain: The tree follows the paper's route from the bank-exchange network through frames, labels, the rank budget, the matrix shear and the power-width recurrence (KS, K10) to the chunk swap (S2), then reuses it for the butterfly layer (S3), the transforms and convolution (S4), resampling and chirp (S5), and assembly, exact recovery and cost (S6, S7), reaching O(n (lg n)^{1-kappa}). It thins out at the label construction (no F^{tensor 3} triple-indicator labels or residual table, so nestedness and L = Ich are asserted, not shown), at the bit endpoint identity, and on the complex side (phase frames C_U undefined, the P_M change of basis only alluded to, s_c < W_c m never stated).

steps.note: The fixed linear network on two banks over three-element subsets, with three stages giving (X_a,Y_a) -> (-Y_a,X_a) and every scratch value restored, is fully stated. The sizes h=100, N = C(h,3)^3 and m = h^3 are never given, although N and m are used later.
A common invertible frame per gate commutes with the pointwise gate, the network implements D_out S D_in^{-1}, and only the edge changes D_v D_u^{-1} cost anything.

Nested nondegenerate subspaces of an m-dimensional space on gates and terminals, comparable labels on every edge, and only the central 3->4 edges decreasing by h. The labels' construction from triple indicators in F^{tensor 3} is not given.
rank(P_V - P_U) = dim V - dim U for nested U in V, with the N source edges 2P_{U_a} of rank one as the exceptions.
Sum of |Delta dim| = Wm - 2N + 2L with L = Ich, and s_b = W_b m - N + 2L_b as the dimension total plus N source ranks.
L_b/N = 100/539 and L_c/N = 101/539, both below 1/2, so the deficit N - 2L_b > 0 and s_b < W_b m.

KS.frame states M_out(rho(w)) - M_in(w) = I_m with frames Phi_M and draws H <- H+D on every row, scratch rows included. Why the bit matrices satisfy the identity (P_{U_a^perp} + P_{U_a} = I_m) is not shown.
A = E_1 Pi E_2, the shear costs exactly rank(A) interchanges plus O(V), and the number of recursive calls per node is the rank sum s.
Children of volume V/W, F_k <= (s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), s/W < m^tau with tau = 1-2^{-50} from deficit > 20*2^{-50} and log m < 20, and F_k = O(e^tau). The exact eta values are not given.

central.summary: All nine steps of the central saving are reconstructed in the KS subtree, in the paper's order: network, frames, labels, rank equals dimension change, the budget Wm-2N+2L, L/N<1/2 giving s<Wm, the endpoint shear, rank-many recursive calls, and the recurrence with tau = 1-2^{-50}. The weak points are omissions inside steps: the sizes h, N, m, the label construction from triple indicators, and the proof of the endpoint identity.
